1. The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in a case registered under Sections 498A, 323, 406 &
354 of the Indian Penal Code; and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2.  Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case and has not committed any offence as alleged.
The petitioner is husband of the complainant/opposite party no.2.

The petitioner has neither demanded any dowry nor has tortured Vivek Kumar Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108175136/
1 the opposite party no.2 for non-fulfilment of the same.

sentences.text: The marriage between the petitioner and the opposite party no.2 was solemnized on 20th June, 2021, however, the parents of the opposite party no.2 did not disclose that the opposite party no.2 was suffering from "epilepsy".
The said fact came to light when she went to appear in the examination on 24th December, 2021 and she fainted in the examination hall itself.

In course of treatment, it was found that she had suffered GTCS attack i.e.
Generalized Tonic Colonic Seizure.
This is the main reason of dispute between both the parties.
Hence, the petitioner may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

3. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2, while opposing the petitioner's prayer for anticipatory bail, submits that immediately after marriage, the petitioner and his family members started demanding additional dowry.
The father of the opposite party no.2 also paid considerable amount to the petitioner on different dates as dowry through online transaction.
Hence, it cannot be said that the petitioner and his family members did not make any demand of dowry.
It has also been clearly stated in the complaint that the petitioner and his family members used to assault the opposite party no.2 for non-fulfilment of demand of dowry.
Under the said circumstance, the petitioner may not be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and considering that it is a case under Sections 498A, 323, 406 & 354 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and there is no requirement of custodial trial of the petitioner, without expressing any view on the merit of the present case, he is directed to appear before the concerned court below within three weeks and to seek regular bail which shall be disposed of by the said court in strict compliance of the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2021 (10) SCC 773 as well as the observation made in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (Supra.), reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 233.
5.

sentences.text: The present anticipatory bail application is, accordingly, disposed of with the aforesaid observation and direction.
